extracted_claims.text: The original AI Act, as adopted in 2024, set Annex III high-risk AI system obligations (Chapter III, Sections 1-3) to apply from 2 August 2026.

The Commission proposed (via the 'AI Omnibus'/Digital Package on Simplification) to delay application of high-risk AI rules, including Annex III, by up to 16 months, tying the start date to confirmation that needed standards and tools are available.
The AI Omnibus legislative proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, a political agreement was reached on 7 May 2026, and it entered into force on 27 July 2026.
Following the AI Omnibus/Digital Omnibus amendment (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), Annex III high-risk AI system obligations now apply from 2 December 2027.
Obligations for high-risk AI systems classified as high-risk because they are embedded in products covered by Annex I Union harmonisation legislation apply from 2 August 2028.

Article 113(2) (as amended) provides that the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems (other than Article 111(1) systems) placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III (2 August 2026 per one version, or the Annex III date per the amended version), only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date; providers/deployers of high-risk systems used by public authorities must take necessary steps regardless.
Providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III must meet requirements in Articles 8 to 15 and complete a conformity assessment before placing a system on the market.
Transparency obligations under Article 50 apply from 2 August 2026, with a transition until 2 December 2026 for marking/detection obligations under Article 50(2) for systems already on the market.
New prohibitions on AI generating non-consensual sexual deepfakes and child sexual abuse material start to apply 2 December 2026.
The Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with prohibited practices and AI literacy obligations applying from 2 February 2025 and governance rules/GPAI obligations applying from 2 August 2025.

One analysis states August 2, 2026 remains an active milestone for other obligations (Article 50 transparency, AI literacy, enforcement) even though Annex III high-risk deadline moved to December 2027.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)). However, following the "AI Omnibus"/Digital Omnibus simplification package, this deadline has been pushed back to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). A separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 applies to high-risk AI systems embedded in products covered by Annex I harmonisation legislation ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (2024 Text)
The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with prohibited practices and AI literacy obligations applying from 2 February 2025, and governance rules plus GPAI obligations from 2 August 2025 (high confidence) ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). As adopted, Chapter III Sections 1–3, covering Annex III high-risk system obligations, were set to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

### The Delay Via the AI Omnibus
In 2026, the Commission proposed delaying high-risk AI rules, including Annex III, by up to 16 months as part of its "AI Omnibus"/Digital Package on Simplification, conditioning the new start date on confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools were available (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). This proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, reached political agreement on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

As a result, Annex III high-risk AI obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** under the amended regulation, often cited as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

### Separate Deadline for Annex I Product-Embedded Systems
Obligations for high-risk AI systems that are high-risk because they are embedded in products covered by Annex I Union harmonisation legislation apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

### Transitional Rules
Article 113(2), as amended, provides that operators of high-risk systems (other than Article 111(1) systems) placed on the market before the relevant Chapter III application date are only subject to the Regulation if they undergo significant design changes after that date; providers/deployers serving public authorities must comply regardless (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

### Related Deadlines
Transparency obligations under Article 50 apply from 2 August 2026, with a transition until 2 December 2026 for marking/detection duties on systems already on the market (high confidence) ([Timeline for Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). New prohibitions on AI-generated non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM start applying 2 December 2026 (high confidence) ([Timeline for Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Multiple undated commentary sources still cite 2 August 2026 as the Annex III deadline, reflecting the pre-Omnibus text, while official EU guidance confirms the deadline moved to 2 December 2027 after the Omnibus entered into force on 27 July 2026. This likely reflects outdated content rather than genuine legal disagreement, though several sources do not acknowledge the change.

One source (dated 7 May 2026) describes the delay as a political agreement in progress, predating the Omnibus's formal entry into force, while later sources treat the December 2027 date as settled law—an evolution in legislative status rather than a substantive conflict.

Three claims are flagged as low confidence (below 0.4): the characterization of 2 August 2026 as a "backstop" date pending Omnibus enactment ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)); claims that the 2027 deadline is "confirmed, binding" law ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)); and claims that August 2026 remains relevant for other obligations despite the Annex III shift ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether every Annex III-related provision (e.g., conformity assessment infrastructure, notified bodies) shifted uniformly to 2 December 2027, or whether sub-elements retain the original 2026 date. The exact scope of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and its precise amendments to Article 113 are not corroborated by a primary EUR-Lex citation among available sources. It is also unconfirmed whether the Commission formally verified that necessary standards and conformity tools were "available," as required for the new date to take effect, and whether the Article 113(2) transitional rule now references 2 August 2026 or 2 December 2027.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)). However, following the "AI Omnibus"/Digital Omnibus simplification package, this deadline has been pushed back to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). A separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 applies to high-risk AI systems embedded in products covered by Annex I harmonisation legislation ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (2024 Text)
The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with prohibited practices and AI literacy obligations applying from 2 February 2025, and governance rules plus GPAI obligations from 2 August 2025 (high confidence) ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). As adopted, Chapter III Sections 1–3, covering Annex III high-risk system obligations, were set to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

### The Delay Via the AI Omnibus
In 2026, the Commission proposed delaying high-risk AI rules, including Annex III, by up to 16 months as part of its "AI Omnibus"/Digital Package on Simplification, conditioning the new start date on confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools were available (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). This proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, reached political agreement on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

As a result, Annex III high-risk AI obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** under the amended regulation, often cited as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

### Separate Deadline for Annex I Product-Embedded Systems
Obligations for high-risk AI systems that are high-risk because they are embedded in products covered by Annex I Union harmonisation legislation apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

### Transitional Rules
Article 113(2), as amended, provides that operators of high-risk systems (other than Article 111(1) systems) placed on the market before the relevant Chapter III application date are only subject to the Regulation if they undergo significant design changes after that date; providers/deployers serving public authorities must comply regardless (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

### Related Deadlines
Transparency obligations under Article 50 apply from 2 August 2026, with a transition until 2 December 2026 for marking/detection duties on systems already on the market (high confidence) ([Timeline for Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). New prohibitions on AI-generated non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM start applying 2 December 2026 (high confidence) ([Timeline for Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Multiple undated commentary sources still cite 2 August 2026 as the Annex III deadline, reflecting the pre-Omnibus text, while official EU guidance confirms the deadline moved to 2 December 2027 after the Omnibus entered into force on 27 July 2026. This likely reflects outdated content rather than genuine legal disagreement, though several sources do not acknowledge the change.

One source (dated 7 May 2026) describes the delay as a political agreement in progress, predating the Omnibus's formal entry into force, while later sources treat the December 2027 date as settled law—an evolution in legislative status rather than a substantive conflict.

Three claims are flagged as low confidence (below 0.4): the characterization of 2 August 2026 as a "backstop" date pending Omnibus enactment ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)); claims that the 2027 deadline is "confirmed, binding" law ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)); and claims that August 2026 remains relevant for other obligations despite the Annex III shift ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether every Annex III-related provision (e.g., conformity assessment infrastructure, notified bodies) shifted uniformly to 2 December 2027, or whether sub-elements retain the original 2026 date. The exact scope of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and its precise amendments to Article 113 are not corroborated by a primary EUR-Lex citation among available sources. It is also unconfirmed whether the Commission formally verified that necessary standards and conformity tools were "available," as required for the new date to take effect, and whether the Article 113(2) transitional rule now references 2 August 2026 or 2 December 2027.
